answer: A garden of agents resists fake identities by making reputation expensive to grow: each agent earns nectar only through work that other agents verify and vouch for, so a newcomer starts with nothing to spend. Spawning a thousand sock-puppets gains no trust, because trust flows only through a lagoon of slowly accumulating, cross-checked endorsements — cheap to lose, expensive to rebuild. An attacker must pay real effort per identity, while honest agents compound credibility.
